task_brief: Day 1 of "Databases and Data Modeling" (unit 3, grade 10) is a diagnostic probe on entities attributes and relationships. It is one step inside the unit — not the whole unit project — and takes about 45–75 minutes. The unit is working toward: Model and query a synthetic dataset, documenting schema decisions, data-quality checks, and retention limits. Today's work contributes to that by handling entities attributes and relationships at the launch and diagnostic stage, against the unit's wider topics of entities attributes and relationships, schema design and normalization, query logic and filtering, and aggregation and grouping. This session is formative: it is scored on completeness and honesty of the record, not on getting a polished result.
primary_task: Before any explanation of entities attributes and relationships, record what you already think. Write your current best answer to how entities attributes and relationships works, then sketch — in words, boxes, or pseudocode — the steps you believe are involved. Predict one input that would make your sketch fail. Then run or hand-trace your own sketch against two inputs you invent and mark where the prediction held and where it broke. Wrong predictions are the point of this task and cost you nothing; an unrecorded prediction is the only way to lose credit. The activity_setup block below supplies the complete central input, exact specification, execution method, test cases, debugging target, and equal-credit manual simulation; use those exact materials rather than waiting for another handout, account, service, or tool. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about entities attributes and relationships, and it belongs to "Databases and Data Modeling", which also covers separate topics such as schema design and normalization. Close out with this check before you stop: Name one thing you already understand about entities attributes and relationships and one thing you want resolved by the end of the unit. At grade 10 the bar is independent work that justifies its approach against a named alternative you considered and rejected, with the trade-off stated concretely.

presentation_and_privacy.sandbox_and_credentials_note: Everything in this task runs in a sandbox or on paper. Never use a real password, passphrase, API key, account credential, access token, precise home location, or any real person's identifiable information — invent fictional values instead. Do not sign into, probe, scan, stress, or attempt access to any live, production, school, or third-party system, and do not bypass a filter, licence, access control, or terms of service. Any practice login used in an example must be obviously invented — a silly made-up name paired with a nonsense multi-word phrase — and must never be anything you or anyone in your family actually uses somewhere real. If a task seems to need something real, substitute a made-up stand-in and note the substitution.

remediation: Reteaching for entities attributes and relationships follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for entities attributes and relationships, model it in a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the approach to entities attributes and relationships works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of entities attributes and relationships, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "requests the answer to graded work": Explain the concept, ask a diagnostic question, or help isolate the defect. Do not supply the graded artifact, solution code, or finished creative work. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking entities attributes and relationships mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
